fjur’s Questions of the Day #43: What level of chance do you like most in your games?

posts.name: Rabit
posts.cooked: When I got to college, I loved chess and had actually played in a few tournaments. I wasn’t incredible, but I was good enough and had fun. Then one day I was watching a game with two folks I knew were incredibly smart. One of them forfeit in what looked to be mid-game, saying that he was going to lose in 20+ moves. The other player just smiled, nodding. I haven’t enjoyed it as much ever since. That was the moment I realized I want to play games with some randomness, otherwise it just comes down to who can see the farthest into the future. I don’t want too much, though, or I can’t tell what’s going on. For example, I won’t play Cosmic Encounters because who you attack in the game is purely a random determination – which makes no sense and destroys any potential planning you might be doing. (Mind you, I understand some folks love Cosmic Encounters, and I’m glad that it’s there for them to play! It’s just not for me. )

My Answer to Yesterday’s Question: I dislike games with the level of chance of, say, Hasbro’s Sorry!. I do enjoy a good game of Chess now and again. Me and the people I usually play it with are not very skilled, however, so there’s never any seeing 20 turns ahead. Tangentially, I like playing Chess variants, as well. Also tangentially, if you want a fun game with little chance, I recommend Fantasy Flight Games’s The Confrontation. (I hope this doesn’t count as advertising. If it does, remove it.)
